purpose: Measure local cold Python subprocess plus wrapper/import/pipe overhead against the same in-process offline HTTP.exchange fixture path used by the owned EXP-073 wrapper. This diagnoses local harness overhead only; it does not estimate provider latency, ranking quality, or adoption.

environment.child_environment: PATH and PYTHONIOENCODING only; no provider credentials inherited or read
environment.network: not used; explicit offline fixture opener only

fixture.case: synthetic neutral 80-card pool from the pinned EXP-073 runner fixture
requests_per_operation: fresh W0 over the canonical first 40 local IDs, with native-order tail retained
fresh purpose-component request over all 80 global IDs

arms.cold_subprocess: For each physical call, start a new child interpreter and invoke the pinned EXP-073 wrapper with the explicit offline neutral fixture flag. Parent captures raw stdout and stderr and validates the wrapper telemetry envelope.
arms.in_process: Use the already imported pinned EXP-073 wrapper modules and call the same EXP-059 HTTP.exchange function with its FixtureOpener neutral fixture; construct and validate the corresponding stdout/stderr telemetry envelope in memory.

phase_definition: Each measured operation begins immediately before creating and fsyncing the pending W0 receipt. It includes pending and finalized call receipts for both serial calls, raw response parsing, local W0 remapping and tail append, full-purpose ordering, exact rational fusion, and fsync of one final candidate-body receipt plus containing directory.

sample_plan.pair_order: Alternating order by pair index: cold-subprocess then in-process for even zero-based indices; in-process then cold-subprocess for odd indices.

measurements: request, response, and telemetry SHA-256 values and byte counts
decision_rule: A separate preregistered transport-path study is materially motivated by this local diagnostic only if median paired cold-minus-in-process phase delta is at least 100 ms, or cold-subprocess p95 exceeds 1000 ms while in-process p95 is at most 1000 ms. Meeting the rule motivates a distinct study; it does not authorize a code change, infer provider latency, correct the prior EXP-073 timing, or make any quality/adoption claim.
prohibitions: No provider, search, DNS, key/environment credential, live gate, lease, or live run access.
No reuse of saved live responses or any measured output for quality scoring.
No adjustment or subtraction of diagnostic values from the prior EXP-073 live phase.
No ranking-quality, relevance, or adoption conclusion from synthetic fixtures.

production_path_inspection.service_lifecycle: The application context constructs the JevReranker provider and the service retains that provider object within the long-lived application process. Calls do not start a per-rerank subprocess.
production_path_inspection.http_client_lifecycle: JevReranker.rerank constructs and closes a new httpx.AsyncClient for each call, so the inspected path does not retain an HTTP connection pool across reranks.
production_path_inspection.timeout_scope: The JevReranker asyncio timeout context lexically covers the request/client context and synchronous response decoding/validation. The server-level wait_for covers awaiting the provider method; caller-side membership and reordering happen after that await.
production_path_inspection.measurement_boundary: The in-process diagnostic arm calls the EXP-059 urllib exchange wrapper with a local fixture opener. It measures an in-process fixture path, not production httpx client construction, TLS, connection pooling, or provider latency.

measurement_limitations: The in-process arm is not a timing benchmark of the production httpx.AsyncClient lifecycle or a persistent connection pool.
The cold subprocess arm measures interpreter, imports, wrapper setup and pipes as a combined local effect; it does not isolate interpreter startup from module import.
Both arms use only deterministic local synthetic response fixtures; wrapper-reported exchange time is fixture execution time.
No diagnostic measurement is subtracted from the prior EXP-073 live phase, and no ranking quality is measured.

protocol_corrections.reason: The first setup-only invocation reached the in-process EXP-059 HTTP.exchange with an empty token; EXP-059 suppresses responses containing the token and bytes membership for an empty token matches every response, so it stopped before any timed operation.
protocol_corrections.change: Use the same fixed non-secret offline-fixture-non-secret marker already used by the cold wrapper.
protocol_corrections.evidence: setup-failure.json records the invocation outcome and verified zero paired operations, child processes, calls, and receipts; no result file was written.
